Removing ambient RNA from a Seurat object with Decant

Compiled: November 25, 2026

This vignette demonstrates how to remove ambient RNA from a Seurat object with Decant. If you use Decant, please cite:

Decant: benchmark-first ambient RNA decontamination for single-cell RNA-seq

Kushal Raj Roy

R package, 2026

GitHub: https://github.com/kroy3/Decant

Documentation: https://decant.readthedocs.io

Overview

In droplet-based single-cell RNA-seq, every droplet also captures some cell-free (“ambient”) RNA released by lysed cells. Each cell’s counts are a mixture of its own transcripts and this soup, so marker genes of abundant cell types leak into all the others. Decant measures the soup from the empty droplets of the raw (unfiltered) matrix, estimates the contamination fraction of each cell from genes its cluster does not express, and removes ambient counts from each cell.

Two properties matter for downstream use:

  • the corrected counts never exceed the raw counts and are never negative: correction only removes counts, it cannot create expression;
  • counts too high to be ambient (for example in doublets or rare high expressers) are kept rather than removed.

Decant needs the raw droplet matrix (Cell Ranger’s raw_feature_bc_matrix) in addition to the filtered cells.

Load data

We use the 10x Genomics 1k PBMC dataset (v3 chemistry), which provides both the filtered and the raw feature-barcode matrices.

library(Seurat)
library(Decant)
library(ggplot2)
base <- "https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/3.0.0/pbmc_1k_v3/pbmc_1k_v3_"
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbmc_1k_v3")
for (which in c("filtered", "raw")) {
    tgz <- file.path(dir, paste0(which, ".tar.gz"))
    dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
    if (!file.exists(tgz)) {
        download.file(paste0(base, which, "_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz"), tgz, mode = "wb")
    }
    untar(tgz, exdir = dir)
}
filtered_dir <- file.path(dir, "filtered_feature_bc_matrix")
raw_dir <- file.path(dir, "raw_feature_bc_matrix")

Standard Seurat processing

Decant uses the object’s cluster identities to estimate contamination, so we first cluster the cells as usual.

pbmc <- CreateSeuratObject(Read10X(filtered_dir), min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)
pbmc <- subset(pbmc, subset = nFeature_RNA < 5000)
pbmc <- NormalizeData(pbmc)
pbmc <- FindVariableFeatures(pbmc)
pbmc <- ScaleData(pbmc)
pbmc <- RunPCA(pbmc, verbose = FALSE)
pbmc <- FindNeighbors(pbmc, dims = 1:15)
pbmc <- FindClusters(pbmc, resolution = 0.5)
## Modularity Optimizer version 1.3.0 by Ludo Waltman and Nees Jan van Eck
## 
## Number of nodes: 1173
## Number of edges: 37289
## 
## Running Louvain algorithm...
## Maximum modularity in 10 random starts: 0.8876
## Number of communities: 9
## Elapsed time: 0 seconds
pbmc <- RunUMAP(pbmc, dims = 1:15)
DimPlot(pbmc, label = TRUE) + NoLegend()

Run Decant

RunDecant() reads the raw matrix, takes the droplets with 1 to 100 UMIs as the soup, estimates each cell’s contamination fraction and writes the corrected counts to a new assay, Decant.

pbmc <- RunDecant(pbmc, raw = raw_dir)
pbmc
## An object of class Seurat 
## 30492 features across 1173 samples within 2 assays 
## Active assay: RNA (15246 features, 2000 variable features)
##  3 layers present: counts, data, scale.data
##  1 other assay present: Decant
##  2 dimensional reductions calculated: pca, umap

Each cell’s estimated contamination fraction is stored in decant_rho:

summary(pbmc$decant_rho)
##     Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max. 
## 0.001861 0.005209 0.006389 0.008079 0.006402 0.213209
VlnPlot(pbmc, features = "decant_rho", pt.size = 0) + NoLegend()

This is a clean sample: the median cell has well under 1% ambient RNA.

Per-cluster diagnostics are stored in the object’s Misc slot. A cluster flagged low_power has too few genes that it clearly does not express (and that are abundant enough in the soup) to estimate its own contamination; it borrows the evidence-weighted value of the clusters that do. With low contamination and closely related immune cell types, as here, most clusters borrow.

diag <- Misc(pbmc, "decant")$rho_diagnostics
diag[, c("cluster", "n_cells", "rho", "n_absent_genes", "low_power", "borrowed")]
cluster n_cells rho n_absent_genes low_power borrowed
0 289 0.0063983 7 TRUE TRUE
1 182 0.0063983 3 TRUE TRUE
2 181 0.0039400 5 FALSE FALSE
3 130 0.0063983 3 TRUE TRUE
4 125 0.0063983 3 TRUE TRUE
5 92 0.0063983 2 TRUE TRUE
6 72 0.0063983 3 TRUE TRUE
7 55 0.0063983 4 FALSE FALSE
8 47 0.0647036 27 FALSE FALSE

Effect of the correction

The monocyte marker LYZ is one of the most abundant genes in the soup. Its mean count per cell, by cluster, before and after correction: the small ambient counts in the other clusters are removed, while the monocyte clusters keep nearly all of theirs.

lyz <- data.frame(cluster = Idents(pbmc), raw = FetchData(pbmc, vars = "rna_LYZ", layer = "counts")[,
    1], decant = FetchData(pbmc, vars = "decant_LYZ", layer = "counts")[, 1])
aggregate(cbind(raw, decant) ~ cluster, data = lyz, FUN = mean)
cluster raw decant
0 136.9826990 136.6707232
1 0.0989011 0.0000000
2 0.1767956 0.0280653
3 0.1307692 0.0000000
4 0.1040000 0.0000000
5 100.2826087 99.8195382
6 0.2083333 0.0000000
7 0.1090909 0.0000000
8 0.3404255 0.0000000 
VlnPlot(pbmc, features = c("rna_LYZ", "decant_LYZ"), layer = "counts", pt.size = 0, ncol = 2)

Correction only removes counts:

raw_counts <- LayerData(pbmc, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
dec_counts <- LayerData(pbmc, assay = "Decant", layer = "counts")
c(min = min(dec_counts), above_raw = sum(dec_counts > raw_counts), share_removed = 1 - sum(dec_counts)/sum(raw_counts))
##           min     above_raw share_removed 
##   0.000000000   0.000000000   0.006410766

Downstream analysis

The Decant assay holds counts; normalize it before use, and use it as the default assay for marker detection or differential expression.

pbmc <- NormalizeData(pbmc, assay = "Decant")
DefaultAssay(pbmc) <- "Decant"
markers <- FindMarkers(pbmc, ident.1 = levels(Idents(pbmc))[1], max.cells.per.ident = 200)
head(markers)
p_val avg_log2FC pct.1 pct.2 p_val_adj
S100A8 0 6.357067 0.993 0.089 0
S100A9 0 5.586000 0.990 0.129 0
VCAN 0 5.279421 0.990 0.081 0
MNDA 0 4.527323 0.983 0.110 0
S100A12 0 6.454857 0.969 0.057 0
FCN1 0 3.979669 0.993 0.096 0

Notes and limitations

  • Decant’s contamination estimate relies on genes that a cluster does not express. In a sample of a single cell type, or when the soup closely resembles every cluster, contamination cannot be estimated from the counts; Decant warns, and a value from an independent source can be supplied with RunDecant(pbmc, raw = raw_dir, rho = ...).
  • Benchmarks against SoupX, DecontX and CellBender, including the cases where Decant removes less ambient RNA than DecontX, are documented at https://github.com/kroy3/Decant/blob/main/validation/BENCHMARK.md.
  • For several samples, pass a named list of raw matrices and the meta.data column naming each cell’s sample: RunDecant(obj, raw = list(s1 = dir1, s2 = dir2), sample_col = "sample").
